subject: Film & Cinema
title: Match Cuts and Transitions
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Match Cuts and Transitions.

hook.text: In 2001, a bone tossed in the air becomes a spaceship. One cut spans four million years.

buildup.text: A match cut connects two shots with a visual or thematic link — shape, movement, or idea.

discovery.text: Kubrick's bone-to-satellite cut is cinema's most famous transition, compressing all of human progress.

twist.text: Dissolves, wipes, and fades are disappearing — modern films rely almost entirely on hard cuts.

climax.text: A perfect transition doesn't just connect scenes — it creates a new meaning between them.

punchline.text: The best transitions are ideas disguised as cuts.

quiz.question: What does Kubrick's bone-to-satellite match cut represent?
options: The entire span of human progress in a single cut
